nodes.title: Discrete-series types and the two level conventions
nodes.statement: Use the imported rank-two discrete-series Weil–Deligne parameters and Jacquet–Langlands representations to form ΦN, its supercuspidal and special sectors, ΦNᵖ (p acts as 1 on JL(M)), and ΦNᵖ_n (JL(M) is trivial on 1+ϖ_D^n O_D). Supercuspidal geometric M has rank two, N=0 and slope 1/2; special M is Sp⊗η with nonzero monodromy. In the 2017 notation Σ_r has level 1+p^r O_D=1+ϖ_D^{2r}O_D, up to the chosen unit in ϖ_D²=p; thus r and n cannot be identified. The quotient by p^Z and its Weil descent are the imported rank-two tower, not a new moduli problem.
proofSteps: Specialise the existing tower and transfer carriers; impose each of the central and open-subgroup conditions separately.
Compare ideals p^rO_D and ϖ_D^{2r}O_D and transport the descent datum, retaining the inverse-pullback and inverse-transpose action dictionaries.
acceptance: A special type is never passed to a rank-two absolutely irreducible Galois-family construction.

Use the strong continuous dual E′_b, acting by (gℓ)(v)=ℓ(g⁻¹v). For functions and forms over C, take the Galois-invariant L⊗F-model before base change to C, as in CDN20 §2.1. The DLB notation E^ρ uses the same Hom convention, not the tensor isotypic summand. Supply the comparison of M_dR^∨ in the trivial-central-character DLB normalization with CDN’s M_dR and ℒ; carry the coefficient line rather than choosing a self-duality.
proofSteps: Decompose the compact-mod-centre finite-level D× action by finite-group idempotents in characteristic zero.
Check inverse pullback, contragredient and tensor-Hom evaluation on generators; retain the two dual de Rham spaces until the normalization comparison is supplied (gap G1).

nodes.title: The geometric period parameter attached to a line
nodes.statement: Let F=Q_p, M a supercuspidal geometric rank-two module of slope 1/2 and M_dR=(C⊗_{Q_p^nr}M)^{G_F}. Put X_st⁺(M)=(B_cris⁺⊗M)^{φ=p}. For an L-line ℒ⊂M_dR define V_{M,ℒ}=ker(X_st⁺(M)→C⊗_F(M_dR/ℒ)), the map induced by θ. It is absolutely irreducible of dimension two and weights {0,1}. The line varies over P(M_dR). The association to the parent’s Galois parameter and to π=LL(M), Π_{M,ℒ}=Π(V_{M,ℒ}) must use a checked twist dictionary: in the CDN20 author copy D_pst(V_{M,ℒ})≅M[−1], where M[k] multiplies φ by p^k. No identity of this geometric M with another paper’s Galois-normalized M is imposed without G1.
proofSteps: Apply the imported Colmez–Fontaine equivalence to the filtration with one line and jumps 0,1; irreducibility of the underlying parameter makes every such line weakly admissible.
Recover the representation as the displayed period kernel; compare the φ=p condition with the standard φ=1 reconstruction by M[−1].
Use the parent correspondence to obtain the Banach object; do not use a geometric theorem to construct that correspondence.
acceptance: Distinct lines give distinct filtered representations even though their unfiltered differential equation is the same.

nodes.title: The filtration-independent differential equation N_rig(π)
nodes.statement: For π smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal over L with trivial central character, use the parent’s set of unitary completions with smooth vectors π and the period-line parameter. Construct N_rig(π) as the descent of the unfiltered potentially semistable parameter through Berger’s differential-equation functor. For every V in that family there is an isomorphism N_rig(V)≅N_rig(π), unique up to scalar, with N_rig(V)[1/t]=D_rig(V)[1/t]. For sufficiently large n, N_dif,n⁺=L_n[[t]]⊗_L M_dR and D_dif,n⁺(V)=tN_dif,n⁺+L_n[[t]]⊗ℒ; hence tN_rig⊂D_rig(V)⊂N_rig. These are the normalized weights {0,1}, not arbitrary weights.
hypotheses: Throughout this supercuspidal comparison, L/Q_p is finite, π is smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal with trivial central character, and the varying nontrianguline Galois family has weights {0,1}; general-purpose function-space and P-finite definitions apply to their explicitly stated carriers.
proofSteps: Import Berger’s N_dR construction, including descent, rather than construct a second generic differential equation.
Apply it to the fixed unfiltered parameter and compare the local lattices prescribed by the varying filtration.
Prove independence by the uniqueness of the imported lattice construction and verify the inclusions at every sufficiently large localization.
acceptance: The quotient N_dif,n⁺/D_dif,n⁺ records M_dR/ℒ and retains the line dependence that N_rig forgets.

nodes.statement: If V is absolutely irreducible, two-dimensional, de Rham and nontrianguline, every nonzero polynomial P∈L[X] acts injectively as P(∇) on D_rig(V), and ∂=t⁻¹∇ is a continuous bijection on N_rig(V). The inverse has the topology supplied by differential-equation duality. These assertions are not made for trianguline V.
hypotheses: Nontrianguline is essential; π-families in GR.1/unfiltered-nrig satisfy it.

proofSteps: Use finite-dimensionality of ker P(∇), then φ,Γ-stability to obtain a rank-one subobject if it is nonzero; this contradicts nontriangulinity.

nodes.title: P-finite vectors and infinite slope
nodes.statement: For a locally analytic G-representation Π, define Π^{P-fin} to consist of vectors v killed by (u(p^n)−1)^k for some n,k and having finite-dimensional span under diag(Z_p×,1). Define the infinite-slope condition by requiring: there exist integers n,k≥1 and m∈Z such that (Σ_{i=0}^{p^n−1}u(i))^k diag(p^m,1)v=0, as in Definition 7.4. Put Π_c^{P-fin} equal to the intersection. Retain these trace quantifiers rather than substituting topological nilpotence of one unipotent.
hypotheses: Throughout this supercuspidal comparison, L/Q_p is finite, π is smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal with trivial central character, and the varying nontrianguline Galois family has weights {0,1}; general-purpose function-space and P-finite definitions apply to their explicitly stated carriers.
proofSteps: Define the finite-orbit condition and trace condition on the imported analytic representation; verify invariance under P.
Compare the trace condition with compact support in the Kirillov model in the next node; this comparison fixes its quantifier form without a new slope operator.
acceptance: On a Kirillov model the subscript c removes all valuation shells sufficiently close to zero.

nodes.title: Locally polynomial Kirillov function spaces
nodes.statement: For a Γ-module X with the t-power torsion occurring in D_dif⁻, define LP(Q_p×,X)^Γ to be functions φ with φ(ax)=σ_aφ(x), a∈Z_p×, and compact support in Q_p (zero is allowed as a limit point of support). Define LP_c by support compact in Q_p×. The P-action is ((a b;0 1)·φ)(x)=ε(bx)exp(tbx)φ(ax) with the action order fixed by the source matrix formula; exp is finite on each t-torsion value. Finite-shell functions identify with a direct sum of coefficient spaces indexed by valuation; LP itself does not.

nodes.title: The P-finite Kirillov model and infinitesimal action
nodes.statement: For the nontrianguline V above, the parent analytic representation Π(V)^an admits the canonical P-equivariant embedding of Π^{P-fin} into LP(Q_p×,D_dif⁻(V))^Γ; on Π_c^{P-fin} it is an isomorphism onto LP_c. For generalized Hodge–Tate weights a,b, the operators on D_rig(V) are a⁺=∇, a⁻=a+b−1−∇, u⁺=t and u⁻=−t⁻¹(∇−a)(∇−b); the Casimir scalar is ((a−b)²−1)/2. In weights {0,1}, u⁻=−t∂². This extends the parent’s P-algebraic fixed-weight model; it does not redefine it.
hypotheses: Throughout this supercuspidal comparison, L/Q_p is finite, π is smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal with trivial central character, and the varying nontrianguline Galois family has weights {0,1}; general-purpose function-space and P-finite definitions apply to their explicitly stated carriers.
proofSteps: Use the parent analytic-vector exact sequence to define the localization expansion and the distribution action.
Apply Colmez’s P-finite expansion theorem and check its compact-support bijection; the full non-algebraic expansion theorem is the exact supplier extension in G3.
Compute the Lie action through the Sen polynomial and check commutators with multiplication by t.

nodes.statement: Construct the L-valued pairing { , }_dif on the two localized differential modules from trace of the t⁻¹ residue, the factor p⁻ⁿ and the σ_{−1} convention of Proposition 7.7. For det V=χ_cyc use the alternating determinant pairing to identify the relevant dual. D_dif,n⁺ is its own annihilator. For the unfiltered weight-one lattice, the annihilator of N_dif,n⁺ is tN_dif,n⁺. Do not extrapolate the printed t^k formula to weights {0,k} with k≠1.

nodes.title: Colmez duality and the smooth-vector criterion
nodes.statement: With the paired Kirillov expansion, ⟨ℓ,v⟩ is the sum over valuation shells of {i_{j,n}(ℓ),φ_v(p^{−j})}_dif whenever v is P-finite of infinite slope and n is large enough. The stabilizer distribution algebra preserves a restricted boxtimes module, and the parent analytic dual is self-orthogonal for det V=χ_cyc. In weights {0,1}, Π^sm=ker(u⁺)∩ker(a⁺); it also equals the P-smooth infinite-slope subspace, and Π has no nonzero vector fixed by the full upper unipotent group.
hypotheses: Throughout this supercuspidal comparison, L/Q_p is finite, π is smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal with trivial central character, and the varying nontrianguline Galois family has weights {0,1}; general-purpose function-space and P-finite definitions apply to their explicitly stated carriers.
proofSteps: Restrict Colmez’s global pairing to the compact-shell model and use trace-residue compatibility to obtain the shell sum (Theorem 7.8).

For the smooth-vector criterion, use the Kirillov model of the smooth π and the absence of full-unipotent fixed vectors; the latter and the general duality formula are recorded as the parent extension G3.
Use the Lie formulas to identify ker u⁺∩ker a⁺, with the infinite-slope condition removing spurious P-smooth vectors.
acceptance: The nonzero trivial representation shows that P-smoothness alone cannot replace the stated criterion.

nodes.title: The unfiltered Colmez sheaf
nodes.statement: On Z_p use tN_rig(π), on Z_p× its ψ=0 part, and glue the two standard charts of P¹(Q_p) with the restricted Colmez Weyl involution. The involution preserves (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=0} and is independent of the line ℒ after the N_rig identifications. This constructs the G-equivariant sheaf U↦tN_rig(π)⊠U as a subsheaf of the imported Drig boxtimes sheaf for every member of the family.
hypotheses: Throughout this supercuspidal comparison, L/Q_p is finite, π is smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal with trivial central character, and the varying nontrianguline Galois family has weights {0,1}; general-purpose function-space and P-finite definitions apply to their explicitly stated carriers.
proofSteps: Obtain fixed-radius control of the dual image from Proposition 8.2.

For Weyl stability use generation after Robba-Γ scalar extension, not generation over the distribution algebra alone; verify both ψ-cokernel hypotheses, extension through (γ−1)⁻¹ and radius control (G4).
Use Colmez’s line-independence of the involution (G5), then glue by the existing sheaf API.
acceptance: The two chart restrictions agree on Z_p× with the same involution for two distinct lines.

nodes.title: Period multiplicity spaces H_M and H_C
nodes.statement: For finite F/Q_p and a finite-dimensional continuous L-representation V of G_F, define H_M(V)=Hom_{L[G_F]}(V,X_st⁺(M)) and H_C(V)=Hom_{L[G_F]}(V,L⊗_{Q_p}C), with M supercuspidal of slope 1/2. The θ-map induces an injection ι:H_M(V)→M_dR⊗_{L⊗F}H_C(V). H_M(V) is finite-dimensional over L and H_C(V) finite over L⊗F. Use the coefficient product L⊗_{Q_p}F, not an identification with L when F≠Q_p.
proofSteps: Take continuous equivariant Hom into the imported period modules.
The positive slope implies (B_cris⁺⊗M)^{φ=1}=0, so the θ-map on X_st⁺ is injective; pass to Hom and the de Rham comparison.
acceptance: The codomain of ι has its L⊗F structure; a scalar-extension decomposition must respect each embedding of F.

nodes.title: The fundamental diagram after taking Galois multiplicities
nodes.statement: For the preceding M,V, taking Hom_{G_F}(V,−) in the strict geometric fundamental diagram gives the commutative diagram with exact rows 0→H_C(V)⊗_{L⊗F}O[M]→Hom_{G_F}(V,H¹_proét[M])→H_M(V)⊗_L LL(M)′_b→0 and 0→H_C(V)⊗_{L⊗F}O[M]→H_C(V)⊗_{L⊗F}Ω¹[M]→H_C(V)⊗_{L⊗F}M_dR⊗_L LL(M)′_b→0. Vertical arrows are id, dlog and ι⊗id, injective with closed image. Completed tensor products are used for infinite-dimensional Fréchet factors.
proofSteps: Import the geometric fundamental diagram, Kummer map, strictness and affinoid inverse-limit topology as the precise geometry contract G7.
Before asserting surjectivity after Hom, prove that H¹(G_F,C⊗̂O[M]⊗V∨)→H¹(G_F,C⊗̂Ω¹[M]⊗V∨) is injective. This is the exactness argument of Proposition 2.4, not exactness of Hom as a general rule.
Use the finite-dimensional H_C(V) factor and the continuous tensor-Hom statements requested in G10 to identify the terms.
acceptance: The left square is the identity on H_C(V)⊗O[M]; dlog has a closed image, not just an abstract injection.

nodes.title: Classification of rank-two period multiplicities
nodes.statement: For F=Q_p and supercuspidal rank-two M, if V is absolutely irreducible of dimension two then dim_L H_M(V)≤1; it is nonzero exactly when V≅V_{M,ℒ} for a unique line ℒ⊂M_dR (in the geometric normalization). More generally Hom_{G_F}(V,X_st(M))≅Hom_WD(M[−1]∨,D_pst(V∨)), and when dim V=rank M its nonzero value is one-dimensional and forces D_pst(V)≅M[−1]. The converse with weights exactly {0,1} is a Q_p assertion; the general-F embeddingwise weight alternatives are retained.
proofSteps: Use semistable descent and φ=p to rewrite the Hom as WD morphisms with M[−1]∨.
Irreducibility forces the equal-rank map to be an isomorphism; Schur gives dimension one.
For X_st⁺ use positivity and the filtered kernel condition, and specialize the embeddingwise Hodge constraints to F=Q_p to recover the line.
acceptance: A character cannot occur in X_st⁺ of a supercuspidal M.

nodes.title: The line extension W_{M,ℒ}
nodes.statement: For F=Q_p, let W′_{M,ℒ} be the preimage of ℒ⊗_L LL(M)′_b under Ω¹[M]→M_dR⊗LL(M)′_b. Put W_{M,ℒ}=ℒ∨⊗_L W′_{M,ℒ}; its right-hand quotient is canonically LL(M)′_b by evaluation ℒ∨⊗ℒ→L. The normalized Breuil–Strauch comparison gives W_{M,ℒ}≅(Π(V_{M,ℒ})^an)′_b, and Hom_{G_Qp}(V_{M,ℒ},H¹_proét[M])≅W_{M,ℒ}. Over general F the source uses a further pullback along L→L⊗F; the Q_p object does not silently claim that general-F identification.
proofSteps: Take the line preimage in the strict de Rham row, then tensor with its dual line without choosing a basis.
Apply the normalized filtered Breuil–Strauch realization.
Apply the Hom diagram to V_{M,ℒ}; the one-dimensional period multiplicity and its θ-image recover the same pullback.
acceptance: Scaling a generator of ℒ does not change the normalized extension.

nodes.title: G-bounded vectors using von Neumann boundedness
nodes.statement: For a continuous L-linear action ρ of G on a Hausdorff locally convex L-space E, call v G-bounded exactly when Bornology.IsVonNBounded L {ρ(g)v:g∈G}. For a Fréchet presentation by seminorms q_i this means ∀i ∃C_i ∀g, q_i(ρ(g)v)≤C_i. The constant may depend on i. The bounded vectors form a G-stable L-subspace; continuous linear equivariant maps carry them to bounded vectors.
proofSteps: Use Mathlib’s von Neumann bornology, rather than metric boundedness on a chosen Fréchet metric.
Apply absorption and locally convex seminorm criteria to sums, scalar multiples and linear images. The general locally convex equivalence is the precise functional-analysis request G10.
acceptance: For normed spaces this specializes to an ordinary norm bound on the orbit.

nodes.title: Étale cohomology is the bounded part of pro-étale cohomology
nodes.statement: At fixed Drinfeld level over C, H¹_ét(M_n,L(1))→H¹_proét(M_n,L(1)) is injective and has image exactly the G-bounded vectors. The same holds after taking a supercuspidal M-multiplicity. The pro-étale topology is the inverse limit of the affinoid Banach cohomology spaces with integral unit balls; rational étale cohomology is obtained by inverting p after the integral global limit, not before it.
proofSteps: Use the geometry contract G7 for Kummer symbols, affinoid Banach unit balls and the Stein inverse-limit description.
The integral global group has a G-stable bounded unit ball, giving one inclusion.

Choose a cocompact free subgroup of the tree action and finitely many representative affinoids. Boundedness on their translates gives one integral denominator for a suitable finite union; the Čech sequence patches it globally (Proposition 2.12). This requires the specific tree-cover input in G7.
acceptance: Independent seminorm bounds in the whole pro-étale space become a single integral denominator only after using the cocompact tree cover.

nodes.title: Bounded duals and universal unitary completion
nodes.statement: If Π is unitary Banach then every vector of Π′_b is G-bounded. For smooth admissible finite-length π₀, (π₀′_b)^b≅(π̂₀)′_b, where π̂₀ is its universal unitary completion. For admissible finite-length unitary Banach Π, ((Π^an)′_b)^b=Π′_b. Consequently Hom_{G_Qp}(V_{M,ℒ},H¹_ét[M])≅Π(V_{M,ℒ})′_b.
proofSteps: Use the invariant Banach norm for the first assertion.
Describe a universal completion by the gauge of the O_L[G]-span of a finite set; bounded continuous functionals give precisely its dual.
Apply the parent universal completion theorem for analytic vectors, with the functional-analysis tensor compatibility of G10; take bounded vectors in the pro-étale multiplicity.
acceptance: The finite-length and admissibility hypotheses accompany the analytic-vector completion equality.

sources.match: States the three bounded-dual formulas.
Applies them to the geometric multiplicity.

nodes.title: Occurrence and finite length for arbitrary finite Galois representations
nodes.statement: For any finite-dimensional continuous L-representation V of G_Qp, Hom(V,H¹_ét[M]) is nonzero exactly when, after a finite coefficient extension if necessary, V has a quotient V_{M,ℒ}. Its strong dual Π_M(V) is an admissible finite-length unitary Banach representation, with all irreducible constituents among the Π(V_{M,ℒ}). No assertion of exactness of V↦Π_M(V) is included.
proofSteps: If no allowed quotient occurs, the period multiplicity subspace in M_dR⊗H_C is transverse to every line. Write it as the graph of a partial linear operator A:S→H_C with no nonzero A-invariant subspace.

Use the linear-extension lemma with prescribed distinct eigenvalues (G11) to embed the pro-étale Hom into sums of analytic duals for arbitrarily chosen distinct lines. Taking bounded vectors gives sums of pairwise nonisomorphic simple Banach duals, forcing vanishing.
For a permitted quotient take the resulting left-exact Hom sequence and induct on dim V; use the abelian finite-length Banach category from the parent for the constituent statement.
acceptance: A non-split extension V with an allowed quotient is included; semisimplicity of V is not assumed.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.15 and Lemmas 2.17–2.18, author pp. 27–30 (published pp. 333–335)
sources.match: Proves occurrence and finite length using a partial-operator extension argument.

nodes.title: Three Steinberg topologies and the special sector
nodes.statement: For finite F/Q_p define St^sm, St^cont and St^an as C^sm(P¹(F),L)/L, C⁰(P¹(F),L)/L and C^{F-la}(P¹(F),L)/L, with inverse-pullback left action and quotient topologies from the imported function spaces. Their strong duals are the corresponding functionals of total mass zero. St^cont is the universal unitary completion of St^sm and of St^an in this setting. For M=Sp⊗η the tower’s M-sector is obtained from the half-plane by the twists η_G=η∘det and η_D=η∘Nrd, with η on Galois groups via the fixed reciprocity convention.
proofSteps: Use the imported induction/function-space constructions, then quotient the closed constants.
Identify the dual by the annihilator of constants, and complete for the quotient sup norm.
Apply the half-plane cohomology computation from G7 and transport character twists through the three commuting actions.
acceptance: The same algebraic quotient written with three different source topologies gives different representation objects.

nodes.title: Banach multiplicities in differentials
nodes.statement: Let Π be absolutely irreducible admissible unitary Banach over L. At fixed p-central level n, Hom_G(Π′_b,L⊗Ω¹(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,Q_p})) is ℒ⊗JL(M) if Π=Π_{M,ℒ} for a supercuspidal M of level≤n, is η_D if Π=St^cont⊗η_G of level≤n, and is zero otherwise. The line ℒ is part of the multiplicity, not an unspecified one-dimensional scalar space.
proofSteps: For supercuspidal M apply Hom to the line-preimage exact sequence, using injectivity of the parent correspondence and its classical compatibility.
Compare with a second distinct line to bound the Hom by one dimension and identify its image as ℒ.
For special M use the explicit half-plane computation and twist; the other Banach types give zero.
acceptance: Replacing ℒ by an abstract L loses the filtration information needed by the fundamental diagram.

nodes.title: Banach multiplicities in geometric étale cohomology
nodes.statement: Let Π be absolutely irreducible admissible unitary Banach over L, with n fixed and the p-central quotient understood. Then Hom_G(Π′_b,H¹_ét(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,C},L(1)))≅V_{M,ℒ}⊗JL(M) for Π=Π_{M,ℒ}, ≅η⊗η_D for Π=St^cont⊗η_G, and vanishes otherwise, with the same level conditions. The isomorphism is G_Qp×D×-equivariant and topological.
proofSteps: Use the completed tensor-Hom and invariant compatibility in G10 to apply Hom_G to the fundamental diagram with closed vertical maps.
The differential multiplicity identifies the period kernel as V_{M,ℒ}; the special branch is the character η.

Prove the source Lemma 5.9: Hom_G((Π^an)′_b,H¹_proét)≅Hom_G(Π′_b,H¹_ét), using analytic-vector density and the completed distribution tensor presentation, rather than identifying these Hom spaces algebraically.
acceptance: The Hom direction is from Π′_b into cohomology; reversing it changes the representation.

sources.match: Computes Banach multiplicities and the analytic-to-Banach Hom comparison.

nodes.title: Galois multiplicities and the vanishing of higher dimensions
nodes.statement: For absolutely irreducible continuous V of G_Qp, Hom_{W_Qp}(V,H¹_ét(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,C},L(1))) is Π(V)′_b⊗JL(M) when V=V_{M,ℒ} with level≤n, is (St^cont⊗η_G)′_b⊗η_D when V=η has level≤n, and is zero otherwise. In particular all dim V≥3 vanish. The supercuspidal dim≥2 statement passes to the direct-limit tower with its stated central sector. The rank-one branch is not a supercuspidal exception.
proofSteps: For dimension two apply the period classification and bounded-dual comparison; for dimension one use the special half-plane sector.

For dim≥3 the 2020 argument follows the finite-dimensional occurrence theorem without a restriction p>2. The alternative 2023 proof, valid under its mod-p finiteness hypotheses p>2, obtains an admissible finite-length Banach multiplicity, chooses an absolutely irreducible Banach constituent after finite coefficient extension, and contradicts the Banach multiplicity computation.
Check passage between Weil and Galois equivariance using the continuous extended action, and then the central-quotient/direct-limit convention.
acceptance: A rank-three absolutely irreducible V contributes zero; a rank-one character can contribute through the Steinberg branch.

nodes.title: Arithmetic completed cohomology at fixed level
nodes.statement: Fix n and the p-central quotient M⁽ᵖ⁾_n. Set H^{i,+}_{n,Q̄p}=lim_k colim_{K/Q_p finite} H^i_ét(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,K},(O_L/p^k)(1)), and H^i_{n,Q̄p}=L⊗_{O_L}H^{i,+}_{n,Q̄p}. The projective limit has its natural p-adic topology; n stays fixed. In degrees 0,1 compare with the integral cohomology over C using the actual Weil descent of the tower. For i=1 the arithmetic image consists exactly of elements whose reduction modulo every p^k has an open G_Qp stabilizer.
proofSteps: Use finite-level étale cohomology and restriction in finite K from the imported tower, then take the indicated colimit before the integral inverse limit.
The Hochschild–Serre edge sequence and finiteness of H⁰ at the p-central finite level kill the H¹,H² obstructions after colim_K.
Pass to lim_k with the integral injections, producing the almost-Galois-smooth characterization.
acceptance: No inverse limit in n appears in the final factorisation space.

nodes.title: Saturation and finite-K invariant pieces
nodes.statement: The arithmetic H⁺=H^{1,+}_{n,Q̄p} is p-torsion-free, p-adically separated and complete, and p-saturated in H^{1,+}_{n,C}. Each H⁺/p^k is a smooth G_Qp-module. For every finite K/Q_p, (H⁺/p^k)^{G_K} with its induced topology is the continuous dual of a smooth finite-length O_L[G′]-representation, G′=G/p^Z. Here p>2 is imposed for the mod-p finiteness input.
proofSteps: Use the saturated injection into geometric integral cohomology and the mod-p^k smoothness from Proposition 5.16 to prove Corollary 5.17.
Embed finite-K invariants into the geometric mod-p^k invariants and use the imported finite-length theorem.

For a compact open H⊂G, the induced O_L[[H]] module is finite over a noetherian Iwasawa algebra; separatedness identifies its given topology with the compact module topology. Supply the topology/noetherianity interface in G12.
acceptance: The invariant piece is compact with the induced topology; algebraic finite generation alone is not the topology assertion.

nodes.title: Cohomological block multiplicity modules
nodes.statement: Use the parent’s compact projective generator P_B, endomorphism algebra E_B and pseudodeformation center R_B^ps. Define m_{n,B}=Hom_G^cont(P_B,H⁺) with its p-adic topology and check m_{n,B}=Hom_{O_L}^cont(m_{n,B},O_L). After inverting p and taking the M-part define m_{B,M}=Hom_{G×D×}^cont(P_B⊗JL(M),H¹_{n,Q̄p}). Opposite-algebra conventions are chosen so evaluation P_B⊗_{E_B}m_B(X)→X is balanced; this is the parent’s Morita convention, not a second projective-envelope construction.
proofSteps: Specialize the parent Hom/evaluation functors to the arithmetic cohomology.
Transport the commuting Galois and D× actions by postcomposition; compare integral and rational Hom using compactness of P_B.
acceptance: E_B acts on the appropriate opposite side of Hom, so evaluation descends to the tensor product.

nodes.title: Integral block decomposition and lifting modulo p
nodes.statement: For p>2, evaluation identifies H⁺ with the p-adic completion of ⊕_B P_B⊗_{E_B}m_{n,B}. Moreover m_{n,B}/p^k≅Hom_G(P_B,H⁺/p^k). The sum is completed as lim_k of its integral reductions; it is neither the algebraic sum nor the full product over all blocks.
proofSteps: At each finite-K invariant piece use the parent block Morita evaluation for compact finite-length modules.
Compactness of P_B permits passage through colim_K.
For reduction-surjectivity, finite length puts a given map into one finite-K piece and lifts it to a larger finite extension at level k+1; projectivity then lifts the map.
Pass to the integral inverse limit and identify the completed direct sum. The parent extension of Morita theory to these noncompact p-adically complete targets is the precise request G12.
acceptance: Modulo p^k each vector has finite block support, while the finite set may grow with k.

sources.match: Proves the evaluation and the Hom-reduction surjectivity.

nodes.title: Finite generation of the dual multiplicity
nodes.statement: For p>2, check m_{n,B} is a compact, p-torsion-free, finitely generated R_B^ps-module. This is a theorem about the O_L-valued dual; it does not assert that m_{n,B} itself is finitely generated over R_B^ps.
proofSteps: Apply topological Nakayama to the compact dual.
Inject the residual socle of m_{n,B}/ϖ into Hom_G(k_L⊗_{R_B^ps}P_B,H¹_ét(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,C},k_L(1))).
Use the parent’s finite-length residual projective specialization and SZ.5/finite-length(c), the finite-Hom assertion of CDN23 Corollary 4.21(c), for the geometric residual multiplicity.
acceptance: The residual Hom is finite-dimensional; finite arithmetic length alone does not imply this geometric multiplicity bound.

sources.match: Proves finite generation by residual multiplicities and topological Nakayama.

nodes.title: Type decomposition, level stability and central character
nodes.statement: At fixed n only finitely many D×-types M occur in H¹_{n,Q̄p} and in each block multiplicity. There are equivariant decompositions H¹_{n,Q̄p}=⊕_M H¹_{n,Q̄p}[M]⊗JL(M) and m_B(H¹_{n,Q̄p})=⊕_M m_{B,M}⊗JL(M). For n≥level(M), restriction/corestriction identifies m_{B,M} independently of n after inverting p. The G-central character δ_M is the inverse of the central character on JL(M), for the tower’s action convention.
proofSteps: Use the finite D× quotient at geometric finite level and the arithmetic injection.
Average restriction/corestriction over the finite covering group in characteristic zero to prove stabilization of the isotypic sector.
Compare the two central actions on the imported tower before defining the fixed-determinant center.
acceptance: Integral level independence is not asserted: the averaging denominator can be divisible by p.

sources.match: Gives the finite type decomposition, stable multiplicities and central-character constraint.

nodes.title: The interpolated Banach dual Π*(ρ_{B,M})
nodes.statement: Let M be supercuspidal and let R=R_{B,M}, R⁺ and ρ=ρ_{B,M} be the imported whole-WD-type ring, integral image and universal Galois representation. Choose a G_Qp-stable R⁺ lattice ρ^{diamond,+} in the R-linear dual of ρ. Write its Pontryagin dual as colim_i V_i over finite coefficient quotients and define Π*(ρ)=L⊗_{O_L}lim_i Π(V_i)^∨ using the parent’s integral correspondence. The construction is independent of the lattice up to the compatible canonical comparison. It has the equivalent integral Colmez description D(ρ^{diamond,+})^natural⊠P¹ (with rationalization understood) and the continuous R-dual of the block-adic completion LL_M,B^{[0,1]}. At each closed x, κ(x)⊗_RΠ*(ρ)≅Π(ρ_x)′_b. The fiber property alone is not its definition.
proofSteps: Import R, R⁺ and ρ, including the empty type-locus convention, from the deformation-ring owner.
Use the stable dual lattice and the parent’s integral finite-quotient correspondence to form the inverse limit.
Prove lattice-independence, continuity and base change using the exact integral-family contract G13.
Compare with D^natural and the universal block-adic completion; the latter is a supplier extension G14, not a fiberwise definition.
acceptance: Both the generic field fibers and the integral inverse-limit origin must be established.

nodes.title: The pseudodeformation action factors through the type ring
nodes.statement: For p>3, the fixed-central-character action of R_B^{ps,δ_M}[1/p] on m_{B,M} factors through R_{B,M}. For M supercuspidal, I_{B,M}=ker(R_B^{ps,δ_M}[1/p]→R_{B,M}) annihilates the full multiplicity module, not merely its closed fibers.
proofSteps: The geometry input gives O(M_n)[M]^b=0, so the fundamental row and bounded-dual theorem embed H¹_ét[M] into X_st⁺(M)⊗̂LL(M)̂′_b.
Choose a G-stable integral lattice in LL(M), complete it and take its block-adic quotient.
Use the Kisin/block-adic comparison G14: this quotient is p-torsion-free, complete and annihilated by the integral type ideal; reduction maps have the stated surjectivity.
Every map from compact P_B factors through a finite-length block quotient, so the two center actions agree and the type ideal kills the whole Hom.
acceptance: Vanishing of the ideal in every closed fiber by itself is insufficient; the integral block-adic argument removes that gap.

sources.match: Proves annihilation via bounded functions and the universal block completion.

nodes.title: Structure of the type multiplicity module
nodes.statement: For p>3 there is an E_B^{δ_M}[G_Qp]-equivariant isomorphism m_{B,M}≅m_B^{δ_M}(Π*(ρ_{B,M}))⊗_{R_{B,M}}ρ_{B,M}⊗_{R_{B,M}}check R_{B,M}, where check R=Hom_L^cont(R,L), with R action (rℓ)(s)=ℓ(rs). The special convention is GR.6/special-family. The topology and duality are those induced by the integral construction and the finite module duals; this is not a formula for m⁺ before p is inverted.
proofSteps: At a closed point x apply the parent Morita specialization P_B/𝔪_x and the Banach étale multiplicity to compute m_{B,M}[𝔪_x].
Pass to the continuous L-duals. Prove these duals are finite locally free over each PID factor of R (G15); fiber identification alone is not enough.

Apply the supplier’s PID rigidity extension (request at R08.3): all closed fibers are absolutely irreducible for the joint E_B,M×G_Qp action. Generic semisimplicity of E_B,M and characteristic-zero trace determine the generic representation. Smith normal form removes denominators without creating reducible fibers.
Dualize back, with check R accounting for the continuous dual of the coefficient ring.
acceptance: The proof keeps the commuting E_B action and G_Qp action; a comparison only of Galois modules is weaker than the target.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.24(ii), pp. 59–60 and footnote 32; Lemma 5.12, p. 54
sources.match: Computes fibers and applies the PID rigidity argument, with local freeness and generic semisimplicity explicit.

nodes.title: Emerton-style factorisation of arithmetic cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix p>3 and n, and take L large enough to define all finite-level JL(M). There is a topological G×D××G_Qp-equivariant isomorphism H¹_ét(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,Q̄p},L(1))≅⊕_{M∈ΦNᵖ_n} (completed ⊕_B [Π*(ρ_{B,M})⊗_{R_{B,M}}ρ_{B,M}⊗_{R_{B,M}}check R_{B,M}])⊗_L JL(M). Only the finitely many nonzero finite-level M-sectors are retained. The inner completion is p-adic with the integral lattices transported from the block evaluation, then p is inverted. check R is Hom_L^cont(R,L), not the recursive dual printed in the source. This is a factorisation of the arithmetic completion defined in GR.5, not all of H¹_ét(M⁽ᵖ⁾_{n,C},L(1)).
proofSteps: Invert p in the integral block evaluation with its inherited lattices.
Take the finite D×-isotypic decomposition and use level stabilization.
Substitute the typed multiplicity structure and use the parent Morita evaluation to recover Π*(ρ).
Check the three commuting actions and the completed-sum topology term by term.
acceptance: At a closed supercuspidal point, the corresponding multiplicity recovers Π(ρ_x)′_b⊗ρ_x and its JL factor.
Modulo p^k the integral completed sum has finite support per vector; an unrestricted product is rejected.

sources.match: Combines integral block decomposition with the interpolated multiplicities; the p>3 hypothesis is retained.

nodes.title: The integral-weight automorphy twist
nodes.statement: For each integer k put E_π[k]=E_π as a topological O(Ω)-module and give it the action g⋆_kℓ=(a−c∂_π)^{−k}gℓ. Negative powers are defined by the continuous automorphism from GR.2/homography. Its strong dual is the analytic quotient that realizes the imported geometric bundle O(k)(Σ_r)^ρ; this target builds the representation twist, not a second generic line-bundle theory.
hypotheses: Throughout this supercuspidal comparison, L/Q_p is finite, π is smooth absolutely irreducible supercuspidal with trivial central character, and the varying nontrianguline Galois family has weights {0,1}; general-purpose function-space and P-finite definitions apply to their explicitly stated carriers.
proofSteps: Check the cocycle using g∂g⁻¹=(d∂−b)(a−c∂)⁻¹.
Transport the geometric automorphy trivialization through the function comparison; check each integral power and the central scalar action.
acceptance: The untwisted integer k=0 recovers E_π exactly.

nodes.title: Weighted analytic realization and the BGG row
nodes.statement: For k∈Z, twist the action on E_π by (a−c∂_π)^{−k}; this is the dual analytic object for O(k)(Σ_r)^ρ with the source’s automorphy convention. For k≥0 prove the strict exact BGG row 0→O(−k)(Σ_r)^ρ→O(k+2)(Σ_r)^ρ⊗det^{k+1}→H¹_dR(Σ_r)^ρ⊗Sym^k→0, whose first map is (u⁺)^{k+1}. Its line preimages describe the de Rham Galois representations with weights {0,k+1}. General smooth central characters require the explicit extension G16; the argument for trivial central character does not by itself establish them.
proofSteps: Define the automorphy action using homographic covariance and verify the cocycle.
Apply the equivariant differential operator (u⁺)^{k+1} and the vector-bundle BGG comparison in the geometry contract G16.
Identify its quotient and filtration by the normalized de Rham row; retain the determinant twist.
acceptance: For k=0 the row is the original de Rham row with O(2)⊗det identifying differentials.

nodes.title: Comparison with the original first-cover formulation
nodes.statement: At the first cover of level 1+ϖ_DO_D, use its semistable model over K=Q_{p²}((-p)^{1/(p²−1)}). The de Rham realization transported from its Hyodo–Kato (φ,N,G_Qp)-module gives the same line-preimage representations as GR.3/de-rham-realisation. Thus the original BS(ℒ), defined as the strong dual of the preimage of π′_b⊗ℒ^⊥, is Π_ℒ^an. The comparison of the two projective-line parametrizations is over P¹(L), and a common projectivity must be checked using three distinct filtration lines.
proofSteps: Use Teitelbaum’s semistable model and the nonproper Hyodo–Kato/uniformization comparison requested in G16.
Compare with the local Galois representation of a weight-two quaternionic form by proper Shimura-curve de Rham comparison.

Produce three distinct global filtration lines by the exact globalization extension in G8. Agreement on three lines forces the comparison projectivity to be scalar; two lines would leave a diagonal ambiguity.
acceptance: The DLB cover indexed r=1 is not this first ϖ_D-cover; use GR.0’s level conversion.

nodes.title: Iwasawa description of the diagonal invariants
nodes.statement: For V in the trivial-central-character π-family, the diag(p,1)-invariants of O(Σ_r)^ρ identify with {μ∈H¹(G_Qp,D(Γ)⊗_LV): for every cyclotomic level m, ∫_{1+p^mZ_p}μ∈H¹_e(G_{Q_p(μ_{p^m})},V)}. This is a free rank-two D(Γ)-module. H¹_e means the image of the Bloch–Kato exponential, not H¹_f or H¹_g; the analytic Iwasawa coefficient uses the source’s inverse-character Galois action.
proofSteps: Identify diagonal invariants by restriction with tN_rig^{ψ=1}, and the units restriction with (1−φ)tN_rig^{ψ=1}.
Apply the exact analytic exponential-image comparison imported from PG.5, preserving its unresolved lattice-comparison obligation (G17).
Use its injectivity and freeness conclusions in the stated coefficient convention.
acceptance: The cover level r and the universally quantified cyclotomic level m are different indices.

sources.match: Identifies the invariants with the analytic Iwasawa exponential-image condition.

nodes.title: Infinitely primitivable functions with component coefficients
nodes.statement: For the p-central cover Σ_r, the functions lying in ∩_{j≥0}(d/dz)^jO(Σ_r) are contained in H⁰_dR(Σ_r)·O(Ω), interpreted as finite sums of locally constant functions on geometric components times pullbacks of half-plane functions. This containment is understood after the compatible coefficient/base-field extension needed to split components. In particular the nontrivial supercuspidal ρ-sector has zero infinite-primitivity intersection. This is a containment, with no assertion that every half-plane function has arbitrarily many primitives. The stronger conclusion that every such function lies in O(Ω) is false when component constants are nontrivial.
proofSteps: Use fixed-radius divisibility or the dense u⁺-power-torsion criterion to kill every supercuspidal isotypic sector.
For the special one-dimensional D× sectors use the corrected component-constant factor and the half-plane differentiation theorem in G7.
To cover every central character use G16; the restricted π argument cannot silently eliminate the missing sectors.
acceptance: A locally constant nonconstant component function is infinitely primitivable after multiplying successive primitives on Ω, and disproves the printed stronger conclusion.

sources.match: The printed conclusion requires the component-coefficient correction and a central-character extension.

nodes.title: Filtered derived de Rham realization
nodes.statement: For V in the supercuspidal π-family and sufficiently large r, Hom_{Dᵇ(D(G))}((Π(V)^an)′_b,RΓ_dR(Σ_r)^ρ[1])≅D_dR(V) as filtered L-vector spaces, up to the common scalar. The derived category is that of coadmissible distribution modules in this fixed ρ-sector. RΓ_dR is the two-term complex O(Σ_r)^ρ→Ω¹(Σ_r)^ρ in degrees 0,1, with F⁰=[0→Ω¹] and the source’s shifted stupid filtration. This statement supplies no Frobenius or monodromy enhancement.
proofSteps: The supercuspidal sector has no H⁰_dR, so its de Rham complex is quasi-isomorphic to H¹_dR[−1].
Compute Hom to the two-copy smooth quotient by the parent analytic/smooth-vector comparison; the filtered subspace is the line specified by the de Rham preimage theorem.
Use the enhanced/derived coadmissible-category construction requested in G18. Do not infer coadmissibility for the entire unprojected O(Σ_r).
acceptance: For the chosen line, the induced filtration on the two-dimensional Hom recovers Fil⁰D_dR(V); it is not merely an unfiltered dimension count.

sources.match: Gives the filtered derived realization in the nontrivial supercuspidal sector.

nodes.title: The boundary-function sheaf
nodes.statement: Let τ_r:Σ_r→the Bruhat–Tits tree be the period projection followed by the standard retraction. For an open U⊂P¹(Q_p), let V(U) be the union of rays from a chosen vertex toward U, and B_i its radius-i ball. Form the sheaf of germs at the boundary by sheafifying U↦colim_i O(τ_r⁻¹(V(U)∖B_i))^ρ, with admissible analytic neighborhoods as in §12.3. Denote it F_π. Its restriction maps and G-action are independent of the chosen origin and cofinal collar sequence. It is a proved construction, whereas its proposed identification with tN_rig(π)⊠− is Conjecture 12.4, recorded only as an expectation.
proofSteps: Use the imported tree retraction and analytic neighborhoods (geometry contract G7) to define the directed collar system.
Pass to germs, restrict to boundary opens and sheafify; check gluing on compact opens by disjoint sufficiently deep collars.
Changing the origin changes only a bounded initial part of each ray, so the collar systems are cofinal and the G-action is well-defined.
acceptance: No map from this sheaf to the Colmez sheaf is declared an isomorphism without proving the boundary conjecture.
